title: Avila Core Qualification v0.1 draft
description: A method owner's scoped statement of where one exact capability implementation's evidence may be trusted: a closed applicability predicate over facts an adapter extracts from verified inputs. Evaluated before a step runs; a claim from outside the envelope, or of unknown position, cannot establish a bounded requirement.

adapter.description: The adapter identifier the qualification covers.

scope.description: A kernel applicability predicate: all, any, not, param_in_range, input_attribute_in, input_attribute_in_range, environment_image_in, fact.

covered_output_slots.description: The bound capability's output slots this record's envelope covers. Omitted (the default) covers every output slot the capability produces. A claim on an output slot not named here carries no qualification assessment at all, exactly as if no record had been bound for the capability: it can still satisfy a nominal-basis requirement, but a bounded or enclosure requirement over it is `CORE-A4402` (or, absent `require_qualification`, informational `CORE-A4403`), never `inside` this record.

fact_kinds.description: Quantity kind for each quantity-valued fact the scope names.

not_after.description: The last instant this record's assessment may stand, normalized `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` so lexical order is chronological. Evaluation never reads a clock — the runner stamps the signed evaluation time into each assessment, and a claim whose record lapsed carries `expired` rather than `inside` (`CORE-A4602`).

supersedes.description: Digests of qualification records this record replaces. An immutable record cannot declare its own death; the superseding record carries the edge, authenticated by its own signature under issuer recognition. A bound record whose digest a bound peer names here is dead: its assessment attaches marked `superseded_by`, but no claim citing it can satisfy a bounded or enclosure requirement (`CORE-A4101`).
